formalDefinition: Partition = <S, I> | S is a set of positive integers and there exists a subset of S, I where the sum of I's elements equals the sum of elements not in set I
problemDefinition: The partition problem is the task of deciding whether a given multiset S of positive integers can be partitioned into two subsets S1 and S2 such that the sum of the numbers in S1 equals the sum of the numbers in S2
inputDescription: S, a multiset of positive integers
outputDescription: True or False, whether S can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
instanceFormat: Format: {N | N subset int} (a multiset of positive integers S; a number written twice counts twice) Example: {3,5,7,8,9,10}
certificateFormat: Format: (S1),(S2) | S1,S2 partition S exactly (each element used once), sum(S1) = sum(S2) Example: (5,7,9),(3,8,10)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the Partition problem
